cards.title: What to expect this week
body: Bleeding (lochia): bright red and heavy for the first 3–4 days, then pink/brown and lighter for about 14 days. The flow lasts up to 6 weeks in total. It can increase when you walk or breastfeed — rest and it should ease again.
Call your doctor today if you soak a pad every hour or pass clots the size of a golf ball.
Cramps (afterpains): normal in the first days, stronger when you breastfeed.
Breasts: first colostrum, then your milk comes in and there may be swelling.
Swelling of the hands, ankles and face is common and usually goes away on its own.

Crying easily or feeling overwhelmed is common in the first two weeks; if it lasts more than 2 weeks or gets worse, it is time to ask for help — it is not weakness. If it feels very intense, ask for help sooner. Source: NIMH (rev. 2023); MedlinePlus (updated 9 Dec 2025).

cards.title: What to avoid
body: Do not use tampons or a menstrual cup for the first 6 weeks — pads only.
No vaginal douching.
Do not lift heavy things or do hard exercise; gentle walking is fine.
Do not stay in bed all day — move a little every day, but rest when the bleeding increases.
Do not wait for the 6-week appointment if something worries you — call sooner.

cards.title: What to watch for (red flags — call today, don't wait)
body: You soak a pad every hour, or clots the size of a golf ball or bigger.
Bleeding that had eased and suddenly comes back heavy.
Fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher.
Foul-smelling discharge.
Severe headache, changes in vision, chest pain, trouble breathing.
Severe belly pain, or the wound looks red, hot or has pus.
Thoughts of hurting yourself or the baby — call 988 or the 1-833-TLC-MAMA line (1-833-852-6262), free, confidential, 24/7, in Spanish and English.

cards.title: Home remedies and self-care (ask your doctor first)
body: Perineum: rinse with warm water from a bottle (peri bottle) front to back, pat dry gently without rubbing. Wrapped ice for the first 24 hours; after that, warm sitz baths. Witch hazel wipes or numbing spray if your doctor approves.
Pain/cramps: ibuprofen or acetaminophen as your doctor told you.
Constipation: water, fruit, vegetables and a little walking every day.
Cuarentena food: broths, soups and warm meals, easy to digest. Oatmeal, ginger, turmeric and cinnamon are traditional at this stage (tradition, no clinical source).

body.label: traditional — ask your promotora
body.text: Teas — traditional — ask your promotora, never a health recommendation: chamomile (calms and helps with sleep; there are no safety data for chamomile while you breastfeed, ask your doctor or promotora first), red raspberry leaf and nettle (traditionally for the uterus and iron; no clinical source). Start with one at a time. Avoid sage in medicinal doses and too much strong peppermint while you breastfeed — they may lower your milk (unconfirmed).

cards.title: What to ask your family for (cuarentena, in practice)
body: "Stay with the baby while I take a nap."
"Bring me water and a warm meal, I don't have to get up." (tradition, no clinical source)
"Help me with the house and the other kids this week."
"Come with me to the call with the clinic."
"If you see me sad for more than two weeks, or I cry a lot and can't sleep, help me call the 1-833-TLC-MAMA line."

cards.title: Gentle movement, Week 1
body: Pelvic floor: you can start gently from day 1, if you feel ready. Short and long squeezes, 3 times a day, without pain.
Walking: short walks around the house; if the bleeding increases, rest.
No sit-ups, running or lifting until your doctor gives you the okay (typically at the 6-week check-up).
